title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: private means this class, not this file
summary: Narrowing 119 members on a real project and compiling turned up two defects in the selfOnly verdict, one of them an offset comparison between two texts of different lengths.

highlights.title: Indices and bounds from the same text
highlights.description: Mentions were located in a text with the import lines emptied and compared against bounds from the full text. A shift of 2697 characters moved a sibling class mention into the class above it.

highlights.title: A test is a use that private breaks
highlights.description: The verdict never looked at the test mentions, so sixty two members were offered for narrowing while their tests used them. An assembleDebug never builds those sources.

highlights.title: Built once per file, not once per member
highlights.description: The blanked text never depended on the member. Hoisting it out of the symbol loop removes tens of thousands of whole file rebuilds on a large corpus.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: A member reached from a sibling class in the same file is no longer reported as used only inside its own class.
A member its tests use is never offered for narrowing.
The import blanked text is computed once per file.
